title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the 1965/1977 manuscript on motives or Dedekind categories that surrounds it. It is page 42 of a typed elementary analysis course, almost certainly a scrap sheet whose other side Grothendieck used for notes; the neighbouring pages are handwritten material on gerbes, Picard categories and 'catégories de Dedekind'. The typed content is the standard homotopy theory of paths used to prepare the Cauchy theorem in complex or real analysis.

(1) Transitivity of 'deformability'. Given a deformation φ1 of γ0 into γ1 on I×J1 and a deformation φ2 of γ1 into γ2 on I×J2, the parameter of φ2 is translated (s ↦ s+a) so that J1 and J2 abut. The two maps are then glued along I×(J1∩J2), where they agree, giving a continuous deformation of γ0 into γ2.

(2) Reflexivity comes from the constant deformation φ(t,s)=γ(t). Symmetry is presumably handled on the previous typed page. So deformability in A is an equivalence relation on paths defined on I with values in A.

(3) Example: in a star-shaped domain with centre a, the straight-line homotopy φ(t,s)=a+(1-s)(γ(t)-a) contracts every path or loop to the point a. Hence any two paths (resp. loops) are deformable into one another.

(4) Remark: a deformation of a concatenation γ1·γ2 restricts to deformations of the two pieces. The converse fails: separately deforming γ1 and γ2 into γ1', γ2' whose endpoints match does not imply that γ1·γ2 deforms into γ1'·γ2'. The reason is that the deformations are free, i.e. endpoints may move, so the intermediate stages need not join up.

(5) Proposition 1: every 'achevé' path, i.e. one defined on a compact interval, is deformable within the open set A into a piecewise-linear route with the same endpoints. The proof begins as usual: γ(I) is compact, so its distance ρ to the complement of A is positive. Uniform continuity then gives a subdivision whose chords stay inside balls contained in A, and a straight-line homotopy finishes the argument.

The vocabulary ('chemin achevé', 'route', 'juxtaposition', 'déformation') is that of Bourbaki/Dieudonné-style French analysis texts (cf. Dieudonné, Foundations of Modern Analysis, ch. IX). It is probably course material, possibly from a Montpellier analysis course, reused as scrap paper.
errors: 'Dans un domaine étoilé par rapport à A' should read 'par rapport à a' (the centre point), a typo in the typescript.

Minor: in the gluing step the parameter intervals J1, J2 must be arranged to meet in a single point (or the maps must agree on the overlap). The text asserts agreement on I×(J1∩J2), which holds after the translation s ↦ s+a; this is fine as stated.

ideas.what: Deformability (homotopy) of paths in an open set is an equivalence relation, proved by gluing homotopies after reparametrizing the deformation parameter
ideas.modern_name: homotopy of paths as equivalence relation
ideas.where_published: Standard analysis/topology textbooks (e.g. Dieudonné, Foundations of Modern Analysis, ch. IX)

ideas.what: Star-shaped domains: straight-line contraction of any path or loop to the centre
ideas.modern_name: star-shaped sets are contractible / simply connected

ideas.what: Warning that separate free deformations of the two halves of a concatenation need not give a deformation of the concatenation
ideas.modern_name: free vs. based homotopy; non-compatibility of free homotopy with concatenation

ideas.what: Every compact path in an open set of R^n is homotopic (endpoints fixed) to a piecewise-linear path, via the Lebesgue-number / distance-to-complement argument
ideas.where_published: standard textbooks (Dieudonné ch. IX, Cartan's Théorie élémentaire des fonctions analytiques)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray typescript page of an elementary analysis course on path homotopy, almost certainly reused as scrap paper for the surrounding handwritten notes. Its content is entirely textbook-standard and unrelated to the motivic/Dedekind-category material in the folder.
transcription_corrections: 'étoilé par rapport à A' reads as in the image but should mathematically be 'à a'.
'a chevé' in the image is 'achevé' (typewriter spacing).
The marginal pencil mark at left ('Σ'-like bracket) and the page number '34' at the bottom left are archival or reader marks, not content.
